style: set the scene in one or two plain sentences

candidates.angle: bahuśākhāḥ, many-branched, names a scattered mind
avavyavasāyinām, of the irresolute, names a mind that wavers endlessly
ekā, one, marks the single-pointed intellect

angle_en: bahusakhah, many branches, of the irresolute mind
angle_hi: बहुशाखाएँ: भटकते मन का अंतहीन बँटवारा

en.intro: Krishna sets up a stark choice between the mind that knows its target and the mind that cannot stop branching out. Listen for the word that names the endless path.
en.notice: Krishna contrasts the resolute mind, aimed one way, with the irresolute mind branching endlessly.
en.next: Krishna now explains that people with this scattered mind speak empty words about the Vedas, missing the truth entirely.
en.meaning: O son of the Kurus, the resolute intellect is one-pointed here. The intellect of the irresolute is many-branched and endless.

hi.intro: कृष्ण एक पक्के निश्चय वाले मन और भटकते हुए मन के बीच का फर्क बताते हैं। सुनिए उस शब्द को जो भटकते मन की पहचान है।
hi.meaning: हे कुरुनंदन, यहाँ व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धि एका होती है। अव्यवसायियों की बुद्धियाँ अनन्त और बहुशाखाओंवाली ही होती हैं।
hi.notice: श्लोक में एक बुद्धि को एका कहा गया है, और दूसरी को बहुशाखाओं वाली। बहुशाखाओं का अर्थ है बहुत-सी शाखाएँ, और यह एक ऐसे मन को दिखाता है जो अंतहीन शंकाओं और विकल्पों में बँटा रहता है।
hi.next: कृष्ण अब बताते हैं कि ऐसे भटके हुए लोग वेदों के कर्मकांडों की मीठी बातें करते हैं, और सत्य से दूर भागते हैं।

en.body: O son of the Kurus, the resolute intellect is one-pointed here. The intellect of the irresolute is many-branched and endless. Krishna now explains that people with this scattered mind speak empty words about the Vedas, missing the truth entirely.

hi.body: हे कुरुनंदन, यहाँ व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धि एका होती है। अव्यवसायियों की बुद्धियाँ अनन्त और बहुशाखाओंवाली ही होती हैं। श्लोक में एक बुद्धि को एका कहा गया है, और दूसरी को बहुशाखाओं वाली। बहुशाखाओं का अर्थ है बहुत-सी शाखाएँ, और यह एक ऐसे मन को दिखाता है जो अंतहीन शंकाओं और विकल्पों में बँटा रहता है। कृष्ण अब बताते हैं कि ऐसे भटके हुए लोग वेदों के कर्मकांडों की मीठी बातें करते हैं, और सत्य से दूर भागते हैं।

issues: meaning_changed: "हे कुरुनंदन, यहाँ एक ही लक्ष्य वाली बुद्धि होती है।" (The Hindi meaning drops the core Sanskrit concept of 'व्यवसायात्मिका' (resolute/single-pointed) and replaces it with 'एक ही लक्ष्य वाली' (having one target). The verse explicitly states that the resolute intellect is 'एक' (one/single-pointed), not merely that it has one target. The Hindi translation 'एक ही लक्ष्य वाली' also incorrectly implies that the irresolute mind does not have a target, whereas the original verse contrasts a single-pointed intellect with an intellect that is many-branched and endless.)

unsupported: "अंतहीन बहसों में बँटा रहता है" (The source text does not mention 'बहस' (arguments/debates). It describes the intellect of the irresolute as 'बहुशाखाः' (many-branched) and 'अनन्ताः' (endless), which refers to a mind scattering into endless doubts and options, not specifically engaging in endless debates.)

contrast_template: "The verse names one mind as having a single branch, and the other as having many branches." (This misrepresents the verse. The source states the resolute intellect is one-pointed (eka/ekā), not that it has a single branch. The verse contrasts 'one-pointed' (eka) with 'many-branched' (bahuśākhāḥ), not 'single-branch' with 'many-branches'.)

wrong_fact: "Next: Krishna now explains that people with this scattered mind speak empty words about the Vedas, missing the truth entirely." (The NEXT verse (2.42) describes the unwise speaking flowery words and delighting in the ritual sections of the Vedas. It does not explicitly state that they 'miss the truth entirely', which is an interpretive addition not supported by the source text of the next verse.)

meaning_changed: "हे कुरुनंदन, यहाँ व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धि एका होती है।" (The Hindi meaning drops the crucial qualifier 'इह' (here), which limits the one-pointedness of the resolute intellect to this specific path of action/knowledge. The source and English meaning clearly state 'इह' (here), implying it is one-pointed in its resolve on this path, whereas the Hindi translation presents it as a universal absolute ('here' meaning 'in this verse').)
